A tracheostomy is most plausibly needed **prior to neck surgery**, because it secures a reliable airway when head or neck surgery may obstruct or compromise the upper airway. The other option, repairing vocal cords after paralysis, is not a standard reason for a tracheostomy, since that is usually handled by vocal cord procedures or by bypassing the cords rather than by creating a tracheal opening. My earlier answer described general indications (prolonged ventilation, upper airway obstruction, and failure to protect the airway), but it did not match either listed option.
